title: Deep Dive III: Unfreezing
blurb: Gradients through a handwritten program. The README asks what happens if its frozen weights are let go. One ReGLU valve worked by hand, forward and backward: open at 0.15, out comes 0.225, slopes 0.45 and 1.5; lower one bias and the valve shuts, and every slope behind it goes dark. Almost every operation in the program runs backwards by a rule, on the real arithmetic, not the rounding. Tag 10, fully differentiable, is doubted from inside the repo: the decisions are flat. Then the one demo that really learns, the learned gallery: you sketch rectangles and 244 weights, from a seeded random start, learn to place the photos on them; a plain-JavaScript clerk deciding who goes where, every pull capped so that far-off photos vote rather than shout, 600 steps a second. A shortcut that snapped the sketch to a grid in ordinary code is refused. Honest scope: a small generic network, not a hand-written program unfrozen; the lab did unfreeze five design numbers (one gradient step solved nearly two moving drag frames in three; about one in four started with every slope at zero); the nanoGPT dream hangs as a question. And the desk's X-ray shows a single valve, dark.

shots.setting: the copper line and a paper control panel · the README's use-cases, 14 October 2026 · dawn
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the offer. A frozen weight is let go, and the README asks its own question. CAMERA: opens wide in dawn haze (lamp change out of ch06's labGreen X-ray: the backlight warms to dawnGold over 1 s), the copper line strung across the frame at 58% height, the Lifespan Rule faint along the bottom. Below the line on a plank stands a small paper control panel (L3), and on it one round brass weight-knob with a tiny inked label 'w' and a pointer at a fixed setting. The knob is rimed in paper-cut frost: white cut-out crystals on its black body, catching the rim light. A slow push in (about 15% over the shot) to the knob. On 'hand', the narrator's hands enter from the lower left on twos (a 'lift' variant: thumb and finger close on the knob) and hold still. On the quotation, a small parchment card unrolls from the copper line above the panel carrying only the README's last three words, verbatim, in a book face, attributed small beneath (the full line is spoken, never set in full on screen). On 'find', the hands turn the knob a quarter turn: the frost cracks into a dozen paper shards that fall and spin out of the haze; the pointer is free. No number changes yet: this is the invitation, not the experiment. The card stays up as the camera settles. (Planted for ch12-s04, where this same card answers the 'why?' tag.) TAG-LINE STAGING (meta staging.tagLine): BY THE GALLERY: the line crosses in front of the learned gallery's stage at 56%, the valves' dark shapes below it; the pencil rests on the stage's proscenium post.

shots.setting: the ReGLU valve on a parchment plate · a worked example, derived by hand from the runtime's backward rule · lamplight
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: one ReGLU unit worked by hand, forward then backward, every number real (derived from the runtime's backward rule; labelled 'derived'). TEACHING MACHINE: the ReGLU valve (art department 23), first seen as a black silhouette against the backlight, then inked onto a parchment plate as the arithmetic starts (style bible §6). Construction: a horizontal copper channel enters from the left (the left value, 3w); it passes a vertical paper sluice gate whose opening height is bound to max(0, gate), drawn to scale on a small ruler beside it; the gate is lifted by a cam cut in the shape of the copper hinge from Deep Dive I (flat, then a 45° climb). Three brass dials sit below: w, g, b, each with a hanging number tag (the forward values live on these tags and on the tray, not in a caption). Out of the right side a tray fills to the output's level. FORWARD: on 'valve' the silhouette inks onto parchment; on 'flows' light runs left to right along the channel, its thickness reading 3w; on 'opening' the cam turns and the sluice rises. On 'half' the dials click to their values in turn (w 0.5, g 0.25, b −0.1; one detent click each); on 'opens' the gate stops at exactly 0.15 on its ruler; on 'comes' the tray fills to 0.225 (1.5 × 0.15), with the product inked beside it. On 'nudge' the w dial twitches a hair and the tray's level twitches with it, then both settle: what a slope measures. BACKWARD: on 'Backwards' the light reverses: a lantern glow travels right to left from the tray back through the open gate. It splits: on 'three' one arrow runs back along the channel to the w dial and inks '0.45' (3 × 0.15: the opening, times three); on 'channel' a second arrow climbs the cam to the g dial and inks '1.5' (the channel's value, 3w, because the gate is open). The b dial glows with the same 1.5 (small, unlabelled in narration). Hold on the lit backward arrows; the machine clacks once per settled number. CAMERA: locked on the plate with a gentle 5% push during the backward pass.

shots.setting: the same valve, shutting · the gallery's own lesson about closed gates · evening light
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: the chapter's quiet moment: a valve shuts and learning dies behind it. A crossfade, not a blackout: the same plate and the same valve stay continuously on screen from s02, so the open valve visibly becomes the shut one. The mood change is played in-shot, as ch04-s06/s07/s09 do: a 3 s tint across the shot's opening, the backlight cooling from dawnGold to duskRose while the plate holds. On 'Lower' the b dial turns from −0.1 to −0.4 (one heavy detent); the cam rolls back down its hinge to the flat part; on 'shuts' the sluice drops closed with a dry wooden clack: the gate's ruler reads −0.15, below its zero mark, so the opening is nothing; the tray drains to 0. On 'dark' the backward arrows from the previous shot fade out on twos, one after another, right to left, until no light runs anywhere behind the gate: every gradient 0. Then 1.8 s of no narration: only haze moving, the dark arrows, the closed gate. On the quotation, a small paper card drops onto the plate bearing only its source and the gallery's cure (the README's sentence is spoken, not set on screen). On 'decay', beside it, a hair-thin paper spring appears at the corner of the plate: weight decay, the gallery's own fix (the toy valve itself does not reopen; no tally is drawn). On 'neurons', far back in the haze, a ghost of ch02's 1943 paper lanterns (two lanterns feeding a third, wiring fixed) fades up at 30% and hangs beside the valve; on 'can', the valve's channel catches the warm rim light again, and the lanterns fade. CAMERA: locked, then a very slow pull back on the last line so the 1943 ghost and the valve share the frame.

shots.setting: the matmul loom from chapter five, run backwards · HandwiredOS's 130 frames · dawn
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: every operation has a backward rule; the whole loom runs in reverse. TEACHING MACHINE: ch05's matmul loom (art department 10), the same 130 thin frames in dependency order, copper threads adding and indigo subtracting, ReGLU ramps and detent wheels behind the frames, mostly empty air. DATA BINDING (style bible §6): each frame's thread count and thread signs, which frames carry ReGLU gates and which carry the 59 boolean wheels, all come from the same export of the compiled HandwiredOS circuit that ch05 uses (made from the clone pinned at 257856e, command recorded in sources.json). If that export does not exist, the threads are drawn at a uniform, plainly schematic density with no per-weight glow, and this shot makes no claim that they are the wallpaper. The real backward pass walks the program's operations from last to first (not the compiled frames); the frames stand in for that order. CAMERA: a slow lateral track right to left along the loom, at frame height, against the backlight. On 'backwards' a band of lantern light enters at the loom's right end (the outputs) and runs leftward frame by frame: at each sum frame the light divides along every thread back to its inputs, each thread's glow scaled by its exported weight (copper threads pass it, indigo threads pass it inverted); on 'rule' the camera passes the gate frames: open valves (shutters raised) let the light through, closed ones stop it cold. At the loom's 59 detent wheels (boolean rounding) the light halts against a small red-edged stop tag: no backward rule unless asked (the same holds for index reads; HandwiredOS has none). On 'arithmetic' the light reaches the far left end and pools at the source table's pigeonholes; on 'rounding' the camera settles beside a detent wheel and its red-edged stop tag (the docs: backpropagation differentiates the intended real arithmetic, not literal floating-point rounding). Hold on the lit, reversed loom.

shots.setting: the copper line over the Lifespan Rule · tag 10, tied on 14 October 2026 · dawn
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: Tag 10 is tied on, and doubted from inside the repo. DEVICE 1 (Promise Tags). CAMERA: on the copper line, mid-shot, Lifespan Rule along the bottom. On 'differentiable' the narrator's hands tie on tag 10 (detent 'tie' stroke): its front inked with the README's two words as a verbatim span of Q001; its knot card reads the README's tagline and its date. On 'doubts' the hands flip it (paper snap): the red-pencil hand enters from frame right and writes on the back 'the lab's own guide · slope 0'. On 'ramps' the camera tilts down past the tag: Deep Dive I's two hinged boards (art department 1), flat, then a 45° climb, corners at 4 and 5, rise in silhouette under the line, with a small brass slope gauge riding the marble. The marble visits a = 3, 6, 100: the gauge needle reads 0 each time (flat boards); then the marble rolls to 4.5, mid-climb, and the needle reads 1. (Show only these four positions: never a whole number at a corner.) On 'nowhere' the gauge reads 0 again at 6 (no card is pinned: the pencil's note on the tag's back is the only text). On the last line the camera tilts back up: the tag does NOT get struck. Its thread drops to the Lifespan Rule at its age as of 27 Oct 2026, thirteen days since 14 Oct 2026: between the unlabelled week and month ticks, nowhere near a lifetime. Because it is still held, the thread does not end in a knot: it ends in a glowing open copper tip with a short copper arrow pointing right (the film's single still-held encoding, meta staging.tagLine), faint and contested. On 'follow' the red pencil is laid on the line's post beside the tag ('rest'), and the hand withdraws. The signature grommet is not drawn. TAG-LINE STAGING (meta staging.tagLine): BY THE GALLERY: the line crosses in front of the learned gallery's stage at 56%, the valves' dark shapes below it; the pencil rests on the stage's proscenium post.

shots.setting: the Huber clamp on a parchment plate · the gallery's gradient for one output bias · dawn
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: far-off photos vote; they don't shout. TEACHING MACHINE: the Huber clamp (art department 24), inked on parchment. A horizontal brass bar across the plate is the 'left' output bias, b, with a pointer on a scale reading 0.5. Below it hang twenty small springs, two per rectangle (each rectangle's left edge and right edge, because this one bias moves both): each spring runs from the bar down to a tiny photo edge, and its stretch is that edge's error. On 'pull' the springs tension; each has a brass collar that stops its pull at 0.08. On 'capped' the long springs (the photos far from their sketches) hit their collars with a click and stop pulling harder, however far they stretch: a spring three times longer pulls no harder than one barely past 0.08. The formula plate inks in beneath on the same beat. On 'vote' the pulls add on the bar like votes on a tally: a small net tug to one side. Then (beat 'adam', on 'shout') a single step: the pointer moves from 0.5 to about 0.492, one notch, the size of Adam's first step whatever the pull's size; the step is inked on the plate, labelled derived. CAMERA: locked on the plate, a slight push on the springs at 'capped'.

shots.setting: the gallery stage among misty hills, training live · dawn
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: learning, seen as unfolding; mostly music. Back to the stage among the misty hills. At 0.5 s the ten photos begin to fan out of the pile toward their paired rectangles, growing and sliding, over about two seconds (the real first fit for the Story preset is 630 to 750 steps at 600 steps a second), then settling into place with small corrections. Under the stage, on the booth's apron, a paper loss chart draws its curve left to right as the photos move. The curve's shape must be the real one: computed by running the gallery's own trainer in the clone (Story preset, default settings, seed 0x517a9e; record the command and output as the source); if it cannot be run, draw the chart with no values on it. Behind the stage, the front ridge of the mistyHills kit IS that same measured loss curve, cut in paper (training step left to right, loss as height; not the kit's closed-form ridge), and the kit's lantern-bearing traveller walks it in step with the step counter, so his descent is the gallery's own descent, the lantern clearing a pool in the fog. If the trainer cannot be run, there is no traveller and the hills are backdrop only. The step counter on the apron runs up. CAMERA: a slow, steady pull back from the stage until the hills, the traveller (if drawn) and the stage share the frame. Hold on the settled gallery.

shots.setting: the copper line, tag 10 still hanging · what learns, and what is still a dream · dusk
shots.visual: THIS SHOT: honest scope. Back on the copper line at dusk, tag 10 hanging unstruck from s05, the red pencil resting on the post. On 'fair' the gallery stage, now small at frame left, is shown plain, with no card (the narration says what it is). On 'unfreeze' a small brass panel of five knobs drops in on threads beside it (lab/drag-knobs: five hand-written design numbers of an app shell lifted into cells); each knob turns once. On 'drag' a strip of 25 small drag-frame cards slides out beneath the knobs, all grey: a stand-in for the frames that moved, drawn to scale (one card per 4%). On 'step' every knob turns one notch together (a single gradient step) and 16 of the cards flip, left to right on twos, to a solved copper face (63.6%); 6 cards stay grey, each with a tiny brass slope gauge whose needle lies flat at 0 (24.6%, every slope zero from the start); the last 3 stay plain grey, moved but not solved. The label sets beneath the strip on the flip. The narration speaks only the two-in-three; the strip and its label carry the rest. On 'network' a small question-mark tag swings in on a slack thread hanging from tag 10 itself (Device 1: a slack thread with a question mark = an aspiration nobody has tested), carrying a plain label: the README's second use-case, not attempted in the repo. On 'attempted' the red-pencil hand lifts the pencil from the post, hovers over the question tag, and lowers it again without writing: nothing to doubt yet, because it has not been tried.
